prompts.text: Name something sold in stick form (like deodorant)

items.quip: A Salvadora persica twig chewed into a natural toothbrush.
items.title: Miswak
items.extract: The miswak is a Middle Eastern teeth-cleaning twig made from the Salvadora persica tree. The miswak's properties have been described by the International Dental Journal as follows: "Apart from their antibacterial activity which may help control the formation and activity of dental plaque, they can be used effectively as a natural toothbrush for teeth cleaning. Such sticks are effective, inexpensive, common, available, and contain many medical properties". In use the outer bark is cut or peeled away, revealing inner fibers that act as bristles. The same stick may be trimmed and peeled multiple times to create fresh brushing surfaces.

items.quip: Scotland's porridge championship awards a golden one each October.
items.title: Spurtle
items.extract: The spurtle is a wooden Scottish kitchen tool, dating from the 15th century, that is used to stir porridge, soups, stews, and broths.

prompts.text: Name a food made by mashing or puréeing (like guacamole)

items.quip: A pseudo-Virgilian poem narrates a farmer pounding this garlic-cheese paste.
items.title: Moretum
items.extract: Moretum is an herb cheese spread that the Ancient Romans ate with bread. A typical moretum was made of herbs, cheese, salt, oil, and vinegar. Optionally, different kinds of nuts could be added. The ingredients were crushed together in a mortar, for which the dish is named.

prompts.text: Name a country with the letter D in its name (like Canada)

items.quip: Smallest sovereign state in the Western Hemisphere by area and population.
items.title: Saint Kitts and Nevis
items.extract: Saint Kitts and Nevis (SKN), officially the Federation of Saint Kitts and Nevis, is an island country located in the Caribbean consisting of the two islands of Saint Kitts and Nevis, in the Leeward Islands chain of the Lesser Antilles. With 261 square kilometres (101 sq mi) of territory, and roughly 48,000 inhabitants, it is the smallest sovereign state in the Western Hemisphere, in both area and population, as well as the world's smallest sovereign Federation. The country is a Commonwealth realm, with Charles III as king and head of state.

prompts.text: Name a device that blows air

items.quip: Han-dynasty China cranked chaff from grain eighteen centuries before Europe.
items.title: Winnowing
items.description: Method of separating grain from chaff
items.extract: Winnowing is a process by which chaff is separated from grain. It can also be used to remove pests from stored grain. Winnowing usually follows threshing in grain preparation. In its simplest form, it involves throwing the mixture into the air so that the wind blows away the lighter chaff, while the heavier grains fall back down for recovery. Techniques included using a winnowing fan or using a tool on a pile of harvested grain.

prompts.text: Name a mammal smaller than a house cat

items.quip: Its interlocking spine reportedly bears a grown man's weight unharmed.
items.title: Hero shrew
items.extract: The hero shrew, also known as the armored shrew, is a large shrew native to the Congo Basin of Africa. Its features are typical of a white-toothed shrew − short legs, slender snout, dense fur − except for a highly unusual spinal column. It has corrugated interlocking vertebrae that are unique among mammals except for its sister species, Thor's hero shrew. This unique adaptation allows the animal to bear a huge amount of weight on its back − 72 kg (159 lb) according to an expedition team.

items.quip: A Lao market find whose family was presumed extinct eleven million years.
items.title: Laotian rock rat
items.description: Species of rodent found in central Laos
items.extract: The Laotian rock rat or kha-nyou, sometimes called the "rat-squirrel", is a species of rodent found in the Khammouan region of Laos. The species was first described in a 2005 article by Paulina Jenkins and coauthors, who considered the animal to be so distinct from all living rodents, they placed it in a new family, Laonastidae. It is in the monotypic genus Laonastes.

items.quip: Brookline's 1989 dial-up service, the first ISP open to the public.
items.title: The World (EP)
items.extract: The World e.p.  is a limited-edition mini-album by Japanese rock band 9mm Parabellum Bullet released on May 16, 2007. The album contains re-recordings of songs from previous albums as well as two new songs, "The World" and "Heat-Island". The album peaked at 22 on the Oricon charts.

prompts.text: Name something that has a saddle

items.quip: Karl Drais's 1817 running machine put a saddle between two wheels.
items.title: Dandy horse
items.description: 19th-century human-powered vehicle; predecessor to the bicycle
items.extract: The dandy horse, an English nickname for what was first called a Laufmaschine, then a vélocipède or draisienne, and then a pedestrian curricle or hobby-horse, or swiftwalker, is a human-powered vehicle that, as the first two-wheeled vehicle, is regarded as the first bicycle. The dandy horse is powered by the rider's feet on the ground instead of the pedals of later bicycles.

items.quip: Its pale clitellum band near the head is called the saddle.
items.title: Earthworm
items.extract: An earthworm is a soil-dwelling terrestrial invertebrate that belongs to the phylum Annelida. The term is the common name for the largest members of the class Oligochaeta. In classical systems, they were in the order of Opisthopora since the male pores opened posterior to the female pores, although the internal male segments are anterior to the female. Theoretical cladistic studies have placed them in the suborder Lumbricina of the order Haplotaxida, but this may change. Other slang names for earthworms include "dew-worm", "rainworm", "nightcrawler", and "angleworm". Larger terrestrial earthworms are also called megadriles as opposed to the microdriles in the families Tubificidae (semiaquatic), Lumbricidae and Enchytraeidae (terrestrial). The megadriles are characterized by a distinct clitellum and a vascular system with true capillaries.
